question.text: Under the post-Finance Act 2019 stamp-duty framework for AIF units, who is responsible for collecting the stamp duty on issue, transfer or sale of AIF units?

answer.text: The investor, by self-payment to the State stamp authority
The Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) of the AIF
The stock exchange where the AIF is listed
The Investment Manager directly, out of AIF expenses

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the Indian Stamp Act 1899 (as amended by the Finance Act 2019), stamp duty on issue, transfer and sale of AIF units is collected by the Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) on behalf of the State, who then remits it. The RTA acts as the collecting agent at each chargeable event. The Trap: Option A (investor self-payment) is the pre-2019 manual mode and no longer applies for AIF units. Option C (stock exchange) collects stamp duty only for transactions executed on the exchange, which is not the AIF unit issuance/transfer mechanism here. Option D (Investment Manager) does not act as the stamp-duty collecting agent. Note: Item rewritten to test a distinct source-backed angle (RTA collection of stamp duty on issue/transfer/sale of AIF units) to remove duplication with Cat III AIF Taxation_30.
